steps.prompt: How far is it from $(1, 2)$ to $(7, 10)$ in a straight line? Can you see a right triangle hiding in the picture?

cards.title: Distance and midpoint
cards.body: The distance between $(x_1, y_1)$ and $(x_2, y_2)$ is $\sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2}$: Pythagoras on the grid. The midpoint is $\left(\frac{x_1 + x_2}{2}, \frac{y_1 + y_2}{2}\right)$.

cards.title: Worked example: a distance
cards.problem: How far is it from $(1, 2)$ to $(7, 10)$?

cards.title: Lines
cards.body: The slope through two points is $\frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$ (rise over run). A line can be written $y = mx + b$, with slope $m$ and $y$-intercept $b$. Parallel lines have equal slopes; perpendicular slopes multiply to $-1$. A circle with centre $(h, k)$ and radius $r$ is $(x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2$.

cards.title: The common trap: run over rise
cards.body: Slope is the change in $y$ over the change in $x$. A perpendicular slope is the NEGATIVE reciprocal: flip and change the sign. Watch signs when subtracting negative coordinates.
